messages.author: e7601c9255f0ba48
messages.subject: CIM results appear unstable
parts:
Dear Karl,
I'm using the cim() function but realized my results are unstable: if
I run the function three times for the same trait I obtain three
different scan profiles and sometimes QTL position move from 10cM to
60cM !

1- I run calc.genoprob
data <- calc.genoprob(data, step=1, error.prob=0.001)

2- I run cim
out.cim <- cim(data, method="ehk", n.marcovar=nmrkcov, window=50,
pheno.col= phencol, imp.method=c("imp"), error.prob=0.001,
map.function=c("haldane"))

Does it appear usual to you ?
Is it due to some uncertainty in the method used to impute missing
genotype data ?
I'm probably missing something so appologize to bother you.

Cheers,
Matthieu

PS: I know you don't like CIM but referees of the paper I submitted
using this dataset apparently insist on this method !

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] CIM results appear unstable
parts:
In the cim() function implemented within R/qtl, we rely on a single imputation at the markers to fill in any missing data prior to running forward selection to identify marker covariates. This is likely where the problem lies for you.

I would recommend looking at MQM (start with the tutorial at http://www.rqtl.org/tutorials/MQM-tour.pdf).

Alternatively, consider using stepwiseqtl() with additive.only=TRUE and keeplodprofile=TRUE, followed by plotLodProfile().

This would be like CIM but with window=infinity.

karl

messages.author: e7601c9255f0ba48
messages.subject: Re: CIM results appear unstable
parts:
Thanks for answering so quickly.

May be an alternative method to fill in missing genotype data prior to
CIM would be to allow using the "no_dbl_XO" ("no double crossing
over") in imp.method available for the cim() function. As this method
doesn't use imputation, this would presumably gives stable results. On
the other hand, this might result in still missing genotype data for
lines having recombination between markers thus, these should be
dropped before analysis. Do you think it would be realistic to
implement this in Rqtl?
Cheers
Matthieu

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Re: CIM results appear unstable
parts:
Dear Matthieu,

I don't like that as an approach either, as it also fills in missing data and then treats the filled-in data as if they were known.

I'll add to my "to do" list the implementation of a Haley-Knott-based approach for the cim() function, but it will likely be some time before I get to it.

karl
